words: Fine. I'll audit the Archive's household records against what the crew actually remember, entry by entry, no skimming. The ledger doesn't get the last word just because it's written down.
Understood. I'll take the agreement as written and compare each household record with crew memory, noting anything that doesn't hold up. Quiet work. I'd rather be accurate than fast.
Fine, I'll keep the ledger by hand. If the point is that nobody gets to quietly rewrite our mistakes, that part I'm behind. Just don't expect me to enjoy the paperwork.
I'll agree to the hand-written ledger, outside the Archive, on paper. A record that can't be edited after the fact is the only kind worth keeping. I'll start it myself.
Gladly, Captain. The Archive carried this ship home once; I will hold its rite in the Cathedral and let that trust be honored anew.
I take up this work with a whole heart, Captain. The Archive kept faith with us once; holding its rite is how I answer.
I can take the memory core checks, Captain, but a full test ties up the Archive access the analyst needs. How do you want to sequence it so they're not locked out?
One concern before I commit: a full core test locks the analyst out of the Archive while it runs. I'd rather we time the checks around their work.
I hear your offer, and I do want the Loyalists and Skeptics sharing a room. But pressing the meeting now could harden the split - may I wait a little?
Captain, I'm not turning the mediation down - I want it to succeed. I'd simply hold off a bit longer, so both factions arrive ready to talk rather than clash.
I'll take the memory core checks. My concern about the analyst's access stands, but the work needs doing.
Fine, I'll commit to testing the memory cores. Tying up access the analyst needs is a real problem - I flagged it - but I'll do the work.
Captain, I accept. If the Loyalists and Skeptics can share a room while this is still a disagreement, we may keep it from hardening. I'm willing to try.
I'm in, Captain. Mediating between the factions is worth doing; better to get them talking in one room now than after positions set like stone.
Understood. The audit of the Archive's household records has begun; I'll keep comparing each entry against what we remember, exactly as it stands.
Still at it. The audit continues until the Archive's household entries and what the crew remember can be laid side by side, without gloss.
I'll carry on with the ledger, since I agreed to start it. Paper and ink, kept apart from the Archive — I want a record nobody can quietly rewrite later.
Continuing, then. I said I'd start this ledger and I will — decisions in my own hand, on paper, kept away from the Archive. Don't ask me to smooth the record afterward.
You offered me the Archive rite, Captain, and I take it up as agreed. The rite affirms trust in the Archive that carried this ship home once; I will hold it at the Cathedral with a steady heart.
I said yes to leading the rite, and I do not take it back. Holding the Archive's words at the Cathedral is the work you set before me, and I go on with it.
